clue.text: This one may do you.

parts.note: to do someone is slang for cheating them, so the one who may do you is a cheat

explanation.definitionFit: A cheat or con artist is someone who does people out of their money.

clue.text: Would you gain the tender creature Unpleasantly cut.

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Would you gain the tender creature Unpleasantly cut.', runs on into 2-down's clue 'Unpleasantly cut.', so its true wording is uncertain
annotationWithheld.clue: Would you gain the tender creature Unpleasantly cut.

clue.text: Unpleasantly cut.

parts.note: to cut someone is to snub them, pointedly refusing to acknowledge them

explanation.definitionFit: Cutting a person dead means deliberately disregarding them, which is rude.

clue.text: Unequal to anyhow a side part.

indicators.note: anyhow means in any old way, so the letters of the following words are thrown together afresh

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a side part in the hair looks lopsided.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anyhow' rearranges the nine letters of A SIDE PART.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are unlike in kind or size are not equal to one another.

clue.text: Took chops perhaps, did they, at The Head?

definitions.text: Took chops perhaps, did they, at The Head?

parts.words: Took chops perhaps, did they, at The Head?
parts.note: reads like cricket or boxing, but the chops were axe blows taken at people's heads

explanation.definitionFit: Headsmen carried out beheadings, swinging an axe at the condemned person's neck.

clue.text: More than one flag is about to rise here.

indicators.note: about means surrounding here, so the two letters of is go round the next word

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A row of flags is about to be hoisted at this spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flag' looks like a banner, but it is the plant: the yellow flag is a wild iris.
explanation.definitionFit: Flag is the common name for several wild plants of the iris family.

clue.text: Part of a dynamo that goes, round and down!.

indicators.note: the word reads the same whichever way you take it, forwards or back, across or down

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Someone describes a spinning dynamo component going round and round.
explanation.definitionFit: The rotating armature of a generator is its spinning component.

clue.text: Likely to entail a good nap.

definitions.text: Likely to entail a good nap.

parts.words: Likely to entail a good nap.
parts.note: describes anything that brings on a long sleep, like a sedative drug or a dull sermon

explanation.definitionFit: Something soporific induces sleep, so it is likely to send you off for a nap.

clue.text: A pinch of tea to chuck around

indicators.note: around means the throwing word is wrapped about the drink

parts.note: to chuck is to throw, as is to sling
taken as written

explanation.surface: A small pinch of tea leaves is tossed about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A pinch' looks like a small quantity, but pinch is slang for theft.
explanation.definitionFit: To pinch is to filch, so a pinch is an act of theft.

clue.text: Is he in the discovery? Yes, all's over

indicators.note: in places the two short words inside the word for a discovery

parts.note: a find is something discovered
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a man was part of a discovery and is told it is all over.
explanation.definitionFit: When all is over, the thing is complete and done with.

clue.text: What! A block in the way leading site? ()

clue.text: Singular form of military outfit:

parts.note: a soldier's kit is usually spoken of in the plural, and this asks for the one-item form

explanation.definitionFit: A soldier's trappings other than uniform and weapons are known by this word, normally plural.

clue.text: It's not mature — yet active.

parts.note: describes a young insect, a grub or caterpillar, that is immature but moves and feeds

explanation.definitionFit: A grub is the immature, feeding stage of an insect before it becomes an adult.

clue.text: Such a cold ruin is hardly stimulating.

indicators.note: such points to the following words being made into a word of that very kind, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A chilly ruined castle offers little in the way of cheer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Such' signals that A COLD RUIN is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lacking warmth or heartiness is far from invigorating or cheering.

clue.text: The sort of idea that's kept to oneself. A guilty establishment 18 ?

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'The sort of idea that's kept to oneself. A guilty establishment 18 ?', runs on into 18-across's clue 'A guilty establishment?', so its true wording is uncertain

clue.text: Cromwell's irresistible horse.

parts.note: horse here means cavalry: the troopers Cromwell led in the English Civil War

explanation.definitionFit: Oliver Cromwell's cavalry in the English Civil War got this nickname from its toughness.

clue.text: A real stinger this implement of chastisement!

definitions.meaning: a creature with a venomous sting in its tail
a whip set with spikes, as in the biblical threat to chastise with these instead of whips

explanation.definitionFit: The arachnid has a stinging tail, and the Bible's spiked whip bore its name too.

clue.text: It's not straightforward, this.

parts.note: describes anything roundabout, such as a route, a question or a hint

explanation.definitionFit: Something roundabout or oblique does not go straight to the point.

clue.text: A guilty establishment?

parts.note: establishment means settling something as fact, here the fact of someone's guilt

explanation.definitionFit: Pronouncing someone guilty and sentencing them establishes their guilt.

clue.text: See 22

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'See 22' is only a cross-reference; 22-down's clue as held is the James I quotation, but the puzzle file does not link the two entries

clue.text: Big effort in the palaestra, in Athens of old.

indicators.note: in says the answer lies within the words that follow

explanation.surface: An athlete exerts himself in a wrestling school in ancient Athens.
explanation.walkthrough: The palaestra was the wrestling school of ancient Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: Exertion that stretches your muscles to their limit is a great effort.

clue.text: Kindly way to treat the loser.

definitions.text: Kindly way to treat the loser.

parts.words: Kindly way to treat the loser.
parts.note: the loser is someone who has lost money, not a defeated rival, and is paid back

explanation.definitionFit: Repaying someone what they have lost or spent is a kindly way to make them whole.

clue.text: Tobacco a. 19 dn, loathsome to the, eye and harmful to this, said James.

definitions.text: Tobacco a. 19 dn, loathsome to the, eye and harmful to this, said James.

parts.words: Tobacco a. 19 dn, loathsome to the, eye and harmful to this, said James.
parts.note: quotes King James I's tract against smoking, which called it loathsome to the eye and harmful to a body organ

explanation.walkthrough: James I's 'Counterblaste to Tobacco' (1604) called smoking 'a custome lothsome to the eye, hatefull to the nose, harmefull to the braine'.
explanation.definitionFit: The king named the organ in the head as one that tobacco smoke harms.

clue.text: A bit sudden, to gush like this ?

definitions.meaning: a short sudden burst, as of speed or effort
to squirt out in a jet

explanation.definitionFit: A short burst of speed and a sudden jet of liquid both go by this word.

clue.text: Cold comfort one gets from him!

definitions.text: Cold comfort one gets from him!

parts.words: Cold comfort one gets from him!
parts.note: cold comfort normally means poor consolation, but here it is literal: ice delivered to the door

explanation.definitionFit: The tradesman who delivered blocks of ice for home iceboxes brought literal cold.

clue.text: In which, as Macbeth said, blood.

definitions.text: In which, as Macbeth said, blood.

parts.words: In which, as Macbeth said, blood.
parts.note: Macbeth says blood will have blood, which describes a cycle of revenge killings

explanation.definitionFit: A blood feud is a cycle of revenge in which each killing demands another.

clue.text: Simply swimming.

parts.note: asks for a plain, formal adjective that means nothing more than floating or swimming

explanation.definitionFit: The formal word, from Latin natare, describes something floating or swimming in water.

clue.text: Anyhow Amos isn't featuring in song.

indicators.note: anyhow means in any old way, so the following letters are jumbled together

explanation.surface: The prophet Amos is left out of a song in some service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anyhow' rearranges AMOS ISNT. A stasimon is a choral ode sung in ancient Greek tragedy.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek drama the chorus sang odes between episodes, each one a set choral piece.
